subject: Request: scope carveout on data-use & named subprocessor - product/security review needed
messages:

Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA - proposed limited data-use carveout & named subprocessor

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Glacier is excited about Redwood for low-latency inferencing. Our legal team attached a redline of Redwood's standard DPA with two asks we need to close for procurement to move forward:

1) Data-use carveout for model improvement: Glacier asks that anonymized telemetry derived from requests (latency, token-level features, and aggregated prompt/response signals) be permitted to be used to improve the service and models ("for service performance and model improvement"). They propose a retention window of 90 days for that telemetry.

2) Named subprocessor exception: They request an exception for one named subprocessor, Streamline Analytics (streamline-analytics.com), to receive aggregated telemetry for cross-customer analytics. They've attached the redline.

Deadline: Procurement would like to get sign-off or a counter by next Wednesday, Apr 7, to keep the quarter timeline.

Attachment: Glacier_DPA_Redline_20270328.pdf (redline PDF, 1 page)

Can you loop in product/security? We need to understand technical feasibility and compliance risk.

Thanks,
Ellen

Team — looping you in from Glacier (procurement/legal). They sent a redline with two asks: allow anonymized telemetry for model improvement (90d retention) and a named subprocessor exception for Streamline Analytics.

Short asks:
- Product: is the "anonymized telemetry for model improvement" ask technically feasible without risk of leaking customer prompts or PII? Can we offer an alternative that gives them confidence without enabling training on raw customer content?
- Security/Compliance: is the named subprocessor exception acceptable with our standard vendor posture (SOC2 + contract)? Any blockers for the 90d retention?

They want a counter or approval by Apr 7. I've attached Glacier's redline. I can draft a counterproposal if you provide guidance on acceptable language.

Attachments: Glacier_DPA_Redline_20270328.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA - proposed limited data-use carveout & named subprocessor

Thanks for the ping. Quick take from Product:

- "Anonymized telemetry" is a slippery term. If they mean aggregated metrics (latency histograms, token distribution counts, error rates), that's fine and already captured in our observability pipeline.
- If they want model training or fine-tuning that leverages customer prompts/responses (even "anonymized"), that creates quality/regression risks and potential leakage of customer content into models. We should avoid any clause that allows training on raw customer content.
- 90-day retention is long for full request payloads; for aggregated metrics 90d is acceptable. For request/response content we shouldn't exceed 30 days and only if explicitly permitted and controlled.

Proposed product-first counter:
1) Allow collection of aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry for service improvement with retention up to 90 days. Examples: latency percentiles, token-level aggregate distributions, error rates.
2) Explicitly prohibit using customer content (prompts/responses) for model training or fine-tuning unless Glacier opts into a separate managed-training program under a Dedicated/Private contract with explicit data controls and opt-in agreements.

I can draft precise redline language if legal/security want to weigh in.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Product

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA - proposed limited data-use carveout & named subprocessor

Appreciate the context. From Security/Compliance:

- Named subprocessor: permitting Streamline Analytics requires that Streamline provide current SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent) evidence and agree to Redwood's standard subprocessor terms (data segregation, no training on customer content, incident notification timelines). We typically accept named subprocessors with the evidence and an addendum.
- Retention: we are comfortable with 90 days only for aggregated telemetry that contains no customer-identifying content. Any request/response content must be retained no longer than 30 days unless Glacier signs a Dedicated/Private addendum that includes stronger controls (VPC, KMS, HSM).
- Training: Security's position is firm — no training on customer content without explicit, auditable opt-in and contractual controls. Even "anonymized" content is risky.

If legal wants to propose a narrow exception, we can put a Conditional Exception Path: CISO review -> vendor evidence review -> legal signoff -> limited pilot. But that will add >4 weeks.

I'll attach our internal checklist for subprocessors and the vendor evidence we require.

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security Compliance

Thanks — this is super helpful. Drafting plan: I'll send Glacier a concise counter today that:
- Accepts aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry collection for service improvement with retention up to 90 days and enumerates examples (latency histograms, aggregated token distributions, error rates).
- Explicitly disallows use of customer prompts/responses for model training/fine-tuning unless Glacier signs a separate Dedicated/Private training addendum.
- Conditions any named subprocessor approval for Streamline Analytics on Streamline providing SOC2 evidence and agreeing to Redwood's subprocessor terms; include a Conditional Exception Path note (CISO + vendor review, target timeline 4+ weeks).

I'll attach a redline of our proposed wording. If that matches product/security, I'll send to Glacier and copy Legal for any contract language tweaks.

Neha

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@glacieranalytics.com>, Procurement Team <legal@glacieranalytics.com>

Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood counterproposal re: DPA redline (carveout & subprocessor)

Hi Ellen — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. We appreciate Glacier's use case. After product and security review we've put together a concise counterproposal attached. Key points: 

1) Accepted: Collection of aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry for service improvement with retention up to 90 days. We'll enumerate permitted telemetry in the DPA (latency percentiles, aggregated token distributions, error rates).

2) Not accepted: Use of raw customer prompts/responses for model training/fine-tuning. If Glacier needs model training on customer data, that must be handled under a separate Dedicated/Private engagement with explicit opt-in, data controls, and pricing.

3) Named subprocessor (Streamline Analytics): Redwood will consider a named subprocessor exception subject to Streamline providing SOC 2 Type II evidence and signing Redwood's subprocessor addendum. If Glacier wants us to pursue this, we'll trigger a vendor review. Estimated vendor review timeline: ~4 weeks.

We've attached a redline of the DPA with the proposed language (Redwood_Counterproposal_DPA_20270401.pdf). Please review and let us know if this is acceptable by Apr 7 so procurement can keep the timeline. If you accept, we'll route the final DPA to DocuSign (link below) and start the subprocessor review if requested.

DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/sections/GLC-2027-042
Attachment: Redwood_Counterproposal_DPA_20270401.pdf

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to jump on a 30-min call this week if you prefer.

Best,
